summary: Scythe is a slow-burn engine-builder where players expand across a hex map, upgrade production, and build mechs, with combat resolved by hidden card bids rather than dice — most games see little to no actual fighting despite the war-torn theme. It rewards efficient action sequencing and territory/resource snowballing over direct conflict, with a long midgame of quiet optimization punctuated by occasional tense standoffs.
praised: Stunning art and production value (Jakub Różalski)
Elegant action-selection system with no downtime for turn-taking
Strong asymmetry between factions and player mats
Low direct conflict but constant tension over territory and timing
criticised: Long playtime for the amount of interaction
Steep upfront learning curve and rules overhead
Some factions/mats considered stronger than others (balance complaints)
Can feel solitaire-ish/multiplayer-solitaire in lower-conflict groups
Bookkeeping-heavy (popularity, resources, stars) for a relatively simple core loop

interaction.kind: territory/area control with occasional combat, mostly indirect blocking

scoring.why: Final score combines stars (achievements), territory, resources, and popularity multipliers, so the winner is decided by a broad end-game tally rather than one dominant track.
